clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of headache, nausea, emesis, and intermittent fever, along with cervical rigidity. Initial CSF analysis showed elevated pressure and protein, but cytology was negative. A second CSF cytologic examination later revealed abnormal cells. Further investigation, guided by the patient's heavy smoking history, included a lung CT scan which showed a nodule in the upper lobe of the right lung. Exfoliative cytologic examination of sputum confirmed adenocarcinoma cells. Based on these findings, the patient was diagnosed with carcinomatous meningitis. He received whole brain radiotherapy and intrathecal methotrexate, leading to relief of headache and vomiting after three months.
